method: initialize → notifications/initialized → tools/list ×2 (read-only; no tool is ever called)

deductions.detail: initialize and tools/list succeeded with no Authorization header.

findings.title: No authentication required
findings.detail: Anyone can enumerate tools. Acceptable for a deliberately public read-only server; not acceptable if any tool writes data, sends messages or spends money. OWASP MCP guidance: authenticate and authorise every client.

findings.title: Wildcard CORS
findings.detail: Any web origin can call this endpoint from a visitor's browser. Fine for public data; risky if tools act on a user's behalf.

rubric.rule: initialize + tools/list succeed with no Authorization header. May be intentional for a public read-only server; it still means anyone can enumerate and call tools.
Per tool whose name/description signals arbitrary execution, raw SQL, arbitrary fetch or file write (max -24).
Per tool whose description contains instruction-injection phrasing aimed at the model (max -50).
Tool name/description/schema hash differs between two tools/list fetches in the same session.
Per tool with no inputSchema, or an object schema that allows arbitrary extra properties and has no declared properties (max -9).
No tool declares annotations (readOnlyHint/destructiveHint), so clients cannot gate risky calls.
Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on an endpoint that is unauthenticated or accepts bearer tokens: any web page can drive it from a user's browser.
Servers exposing zero tools score on the checks that still apply; this is reported, not penalised.

limits: Black-box and read-only: no tool is invoked, so tool behaviour (injection handling, authz inside tools) is NOT tested.
Rug-pull check compares two fetches ~1.5s apart in one session. It catches servers that change definitions dynamically, not a change made next week. Store the per-tool hashes and re-scan to pin.
Poisoning and broad-tool checks are heuristics (name/description regexes). Expect false positives and misses.
A high score is not a certification of safety.
note: Scanned from a sandbox whose resolver maps hosts to 198.18.0.0/15; SSRF guard bypassed for this CLI run only.
